On 2026-05-18 04:12, Sion Buckler wrote:

Mr Egan,

Further to my previous correspondence, I understand that matters concerning the property and family were discussed by Llandough Community Council in or around 1988 and that my late father William "Billy" Buckler addressed the Council.

I am attempting to reconstruct the historical chain of occupation, ownership, administration and public record concerning the property, family and associated farm lands. 

https://bpvsbuckler.datro.xyz

Accordingly, I request disclosure of all records held by Llandough Community Council, regardless of date, concerning:

  • Ty Mawr (Great House), Llandough;
  • the associated farm lands and any connected parcels;
  • the Williams family and successors in occupation;
  • Billy Buckler, Branwen Buckler and members of the Buckler family;
  • historical ownership, occupation, tenancy, possession, planning, access, acquisition, disposal, development, disputes or representations;
  • BP v Buckler and related matters;
  • any meetings in which Billy Buckler addressed the Council.

This request includes, but is not limited to:

  • minute books;
  • agendas;
  • correspondence;
  • maps;
  • plans;
  • asset registers;
  • committee papers;
  • land schedules;
  • photographs;
  • memoranda;
  • clerk notes;
  • archived files;
  • transferred records;
  • records held by third-party archives on the Council's behalf.

If records predating the present Council are not held, please confirm:

  1. Whether older records were transferred elsewhere;
  2. The archive location;
  3. Whether records were destroyed and under what retention policy;
  4. The earliest records held concerning the property.

My understanding is that family occupation and acquisition history extends substantially earlier, potentially to the seventeenth century, and I am seeking to establish the documentary chain.

I am confident that our claim to the fee simple absolute manorial title still stands and no amount of time, fraud, purgergy, court "mistakes", gaps in records, demolition of our home, erasure of history (like Marconi staying with us while inventing radio), acts of terrorism, human rights violations, lawfare, nor proceedural unfairness and supression or witholding of information and possible murder of members of my family has changed that fact. It appears our title was stolen and this is a position grandmother held until 1982 when she conveniently died in the 2 week window she had to challenge BP's registrstion of our land in their name with the land registry. 

ITV also recently declassified and published coverage too: 

https://youtu.be/4GXmR7mAas0?feature=shared

This is a terrorist/ hostage situation so far as I see. My dispossessed family are your hostages not constituents. They are too frightened to even speak up about this matter. I require of your department some effort to revisit your postion. 

My research tells me that the councillor at the time said, prior to my father's death, that the situation with BP would result in a death. I believe that was concerning the conflict with Bailiffs, Police and possibly SAS. 

I have submitted a FOI to the MOD too. The Ministry of Justice are also on notice and imply this matter is being investigated. 

If not me, who? If not now, when?

My address is 5 Robin Hill, Dinas Powys, Vale of Glamorgan, CF64 4TF. If you care to visit or write or deliver items, please do so to that address. 

Kind regards,


Sion Buckler Esq. (Ret'd Sergeant)

From: Sion Buckler <hywelapbuckler@gmail.com>
Sent: 14 November 2025 12:49
To: kanishka.narayan.mp@parliament.uk
Subject: BP vs Buckler

 

Sir/Ma'am,

I am your constituent, living in Dinas Powys. I am writing to request your assistance in reviewing a historic legal matter involving my family: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler (1987), relating to Great House Farm, Llandough.

My family lived on, cared for and claimed to own that farm for generations. The events surrounding the 1987 case resulted in the loss of our home and land, and left several members of my family deeply affected. Recent research I have undertaken has revealed significant procedural inconsistencies, historical irregularities, unanswered questions regarding corporate identity, unverified service of key documents, and heritage considerations relating to the site.

I have attached a short report summarising SOME of these issues. I am requesting your help in identifying the appropriate bodies—legal, historical, or governmental—who may be able to independently review the historical record to ensure fairness, accuracy, and transparency.

My interest is not solely personal; Great House Farm has a heritage significance to Wales, including documented accounts that Guglielmo Marconi stayed there while experimenting with early radio technology. I believe this should form part of our preserved historical record.

By way of background, I am a veteran and have served both in the Armed Forces and recently with the Vale of Glamorgan Council. My intention is simply to seek clarity, proper review, and justice where appropriate. I would be grateful for your guidance on the correct avenues to pursue.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to your response.

Yours sincerely,


Sion Buckler
5 Robin Hill
Dinas Powys
CF64 4TF
Tel: 0203 137 7118
